🔗 Combined Admission Analysis — Portal Records Cross-Matched with EXTRAEDGE Leads
Every confirmed admission from Admission1 + Admission2 (Digital Campus / NeverSkip Portal) is matched against the Touched Leads sheet using primary mobile, secondary mobile, WhatsApp number, email ID, father's/mother's contact & email. This reveals: admissions present in the Portal but missing from Leads (no EXTRAEDGE lead record), admissions present in Leads (Stage = 08-Admission Completed) but missing from the Portal (not yet synced), and admissions confirmed in both — for which we can identify the Lead Owner / Counsellor.

⚠️ Data Quality — Process Gap Analysis
Process: every admission must originate as a LeadId in EXTRAEDGE, progress to Stage 08-Admission Completed, then be uploaded to Digital Campus / NeverSkip Portal. Two gap types are tracked below: (1) "Not Uploaded to Portal" — Lead Owner marked the admission complete in EXTRAEDGE but the student record doesn't exist in the Portal yet; (2) "No LeadId Found" — student is enrolled in the Portal but no matching EXTRAEDGE lead (by phone, email, or name+branch) was found, so the Lead Owner is unidentifiable.

PTM · every branch, every response

By grade group — ratings, spread and categories

The same cut the printed PTM reports use: each grade group with its own star distribution, average out of 5 and satisfaction percentage, then the overall spread, the category scores and what parents praised against what they raised.

Satisfaction, inside each questionnaire

Branches are grouped by the form their parents actually filled in. Compare down a block; do not compare across blocks.

What parents wrote — the layer that is comparable

The same language model read every branch's comments, so these rates mean the same thing everywhere. This is the table to manage by.

Which concerns cluster where

Shaded by how far each count sits from what that branch's overall share of concerns would predict — so a busy branch does not simply look worse everywhere.

What moves a parent's overall score

Correlation between each part of the school experience and the parent's own overall rating, run inside a single questionnaire at a time.

Where the rating and the words disagree

Responses whose score and wording point in opposite directions.

Month on month, each branch against itself

The questionnaire is held constant, so the movement here is real.

The action queue — 0 escalated items

Everything at P1 or P2, highest priority first, with the owner the pipeline suggests.

Where the work would land

Escalated items grouped by the owner the pipeline suggests.

How far to trust this data

What was collected, what was flagged, and the one change that would make the whole page stronger.

In parents' own words — 0 comments

Every substantive comment, most negative first. The search box above filters this too.

School Audit Tracker

Loading…
All branches · All months
Reading the audit sheet…
School Audit · every branch, every month

Branch scorecard

Compliance is Yes ÷ (Yes + No + IP) across the five stage columns — the same formula the branch sheets use in their own OVERALL COMPLIANCE SCORE row. NA and NR are excluded from the denominator rather than counted against a branch. In progress counts as a miss: unfinished work at audit time is not compliance, and half-crediting it would let a branch sit at 50% permanently by never closing anything.

Month on month

Every branch against the 85% on-track line and the 65% review line.

Where the gaps actually are

Each of the thirteen audit sections, for every branch. This is the one view that separates a branch problem from a policy problem.

Stage by stage, branch against branch

Branches across the top, one stage at a time. Tap a stage to open the thirteen audit sections beneath it.

By stage

The same checklist scored across Prep to 9–10, network-wide. A stage that trails the others everywhere usually means the SOP was written for the rest of the school and never adapted to it.

Failing twice running

Items below half in both of the last two audits. This is the action list: everything here has already been flagged once and has not moved.

What moved

Changes of 20 points or more since the previous audit, in both directions.

The weakest checklist items network-wide

Ranked across every branch and month together, so a low score here is a group-level finding rather than one campus having a bad month.

How far to trust these numbers

A compliance percentage only speaks for the part of the checklist that was actually scored. This section shows how much that is, branch by branch.

What the auditors wrote — 0 observations

The qualitative record, lowest-scoring items first. These are usually more actionable than any percentage on this page.
